prize_parts.citation: For establishing liquid-liquid phase separation as a physical-chemical principle that organizes the interior of living cells.

statement.case_for: Phase separation is the one shortlisted candidate that is both a new organizing principle and a physical-chemistry result in the strict sense. Brangwynne and Hyman showed in 2009 that P granules behave as liquids, and the nucleolus work followed. Rosen then supplied the quantitative multivalency framework in reconstituted systems, with phase diagrams and valency-dependent thresholds that can be tested against experiment. That link between theory and measurement is my standard for a prize. The consequences are already visible in cell biology, neurodegeneration and drug-discovery programmes aimed at condensates. A three-person cut is defensible: the founding observation is two people, and the quantitative chemical framework is a third.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is maturity. It is still contested which in-vivo condensates are genuinely phase-separated liquids and which are other assemblies, and links to function are uneven. Some of the chemistry also sits closer to biology than to chemistry. Pappu and Mittag, who worked out sequence grammar and theory, would be left out, and that exclusion would be criticised. If the committee judges that the field has not yet settled which cellular structures are true condensates, PROTACs or base editing offer firmer, clinically visible consequences.

responses.point: Base editing (B006) should rank first: it is a clear chemical invention, deaminase chemistry fused to a Cas9 nickase, with directed evolution of the adenine editor and early clinical use, and a Liu-led trio is attributable.
responses.response: I agree base editing is a real game-changer and the chemistry is explicit. My worry is attribution and novelty. Kondo and Nishida's parallel cytidine-deaminase work complicates the cleaner Liu, Komor and Gaudelli trio. The 2020 CRISPR prize also means the increment will be questioned, and a prize here would probably have to absorb prime editing for Liu. I would not put it first, but I would keep it as a serious alternative, and if you can show that priority is clean I could move it up.

responses.point: Nanopore sensing (B048) is first for its clean physical principle and a decisive ratcheting step, and phase separation is second but slightly early because of the debate over what is truly phase-separated.
responses.response: I accept the maturity point on phase separation and have made it my main reservation. The concept has been reproduced by many independent groups, and the debate is about which cellular structures qualify, not about whether liquid-liquid demixing can organize a cytoplasm. For nanopores I share your difficulty with five claimants, and the ratchet step by Akeson and the engineered pore by Bayley, with Deamer and Branton as originators, do not reduce to three names without discarding a real contributor. That attribution problem is why I keep nanopores off my own list for now.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B017) are first, because lipid self-assembly and phase behaviour became medicines at global scale, with phase separation second.
responses.response: I respect that the lipid chemistry is real and the consequences are enormous. My concern is a split between the Vancouver lineage (Cullis, Hope, Madden) and the MIT lineage (Anderson, Langer), plus MacLachlan, in a field where the 2023 Medicine prize already rewarded the mRNA side. That would make a clean three-person cut hard and invite a credit dispute. It is a close call, and I would like to hear whether you can give a precise attribution of the ionizable-lipid step.

responses.point: Induced-proximity degraders (B068) rank first, as a design principle that expands the druggable proteome, with Handa's cereblon work explaining molecular glues.
responses.response: I share your enthusiasm for B068 and ranked it second. I would separate the Crews and Deshaies PROTAC concept, with Ciulli's VHL and ternary-complex work, from the cereblon glue strand. Handa's contribution is mechanistic, not a design invention, and a single citation spanning both strands risks being vague. The absence so far of an approved heterobifunctional PROTAC makes me think the timing is a little early, though I do not consider it premature.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards the debate over which cellular condensates are truly phase-separated as disqualifying or merely as normal open questions in a young field.
Whether a Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen trio can be defended against Pappu and Mittag, whose theory of sequence grammar is arguably as much a part of the chemistry as the founding observations.
Whether the Kondo and Nishida priority claim materially weakens base editing, and how heavily the 2020 CRISPR prize should count against it.
Whether PROTACs should wait for an approved heterobifunctional degrader.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the preferred configuration or the named alternatives: my Warshel and EVB connections and my Uppsala ribosome and RNA community ties do not touch the credited people. I note only that my own work on free-energy and binding simulation gives me a bias toward results that connect quantitatively to experiment.
